messages:
Alyssa: Heads up — noticed 3 tenants got ejected from the Dedicated pool this morning during a ~6m traffic spike. Logs show errors: `reserved_throughput_exceeded` and `tenant_isolation_violation`. Anyone else see this?

Matt: Saw the alert. Confirmed — burst credits drained and ejection logic kicked in. Current behavior: on breach >2s we eject tenant for 15m. Is that still what we want?

Jia: From telemetry the pattern was an 800rps burst sustained ~45s -> token bucket drained. Seems noisy but short. Can we add a short pre-ejection grace window (e.g., 60s) to avoid unnecessary hard ejections? :thinking:   

Alyssa: Proposed: introduce a "soft-throttle" state that lasts up to 2m and routes traffic to fallback (if allowed) before full ejection. Also update console to show "soft-throttled" status and reason.

Sam: Routing note — fallback to hosted is problematic for some customers (data/privacy). Soft-throttle must be opt-in per-tenant (or disabled by contract). Console toggle + API flag required.

Matt: Implementation ideas: (1) expand token-bucket to include a 60s grace buffer, or (2) add a `soft_eject` flag that emits a different 429 variant (e.g., 429G) with `Retry-After` and triggers fallback. Leaning to option 2 because it's explicit and easier to trace in logs.

Jia: We also need new telemetry: `count_soft_ejects`, `avg_soft_duration_s`, `soft_to_hard_transition_rate`. Dashboards should show per-tenant timeline and a heatmap of soft->hard transitions. Add alert: if soft->hard transition >1% over 1h, page oncall.

Leo: From contract / legal POV — routing to hosted is only allowed for non-enterprise tenants unless explicitly permitted. Console must surface a migration-allowed flag and routing must check that at enforcement time.

Alyssa: Agreed. Rollout plan: API + telemetry first, UX next. Feature-flag this behind `soft-eject-v1`. Small experiment: enable for 10% of Dedicated pods next week, monitor soft->hard transition and user reports.

Matt: Config sketch I can implement quickly: 

```json
{
  "reserved_throughput": 200,
  "burst_tokens": 1000,
  "soft_eject": {
    "enabled": true,
    "grace_window_s": 60,
    "max_soft_duration_s": 120
  }
}
```

Jia: Perf caution — if we fallback often we risk KV-cache churn. Sticky routing for ~10s during soft state would help reduce repeated cold starts.

deploy-bot: Incident acknowledged. Runbook: https://wiki/redwood/runbooks/dedicated-quota  

Sam: I'll mock console UX and drop screenshots in #design. Will add an explicit "allow fallback" toggle and a per-tenant history timeline.

Alyssa: I'll own the rollout doc + experiment criteria (SLO metrics, alert thresholds, rollback conditions). Thanks all :thumbsup:

Matt: One more question — what should the API return in soft state? Keep 200 with `x-soft-throttle: true` or 429G? Thoughts?

Jia: Prefer 429G + body explaining fallback option; gives clear signals to clients to backoff. But add smoothing header for clients that can't parse custom codes.

Leo: Add a note to sales/CS playbook so they can pre-warn affected customers when we flip the experiment.

Alyssa: Added to my rollout checklist. We'll sync tomorrow at 10 for a quick plan if anyone wants to join.
